title: Physical and Chemical Change
seo_title: Grade 10 Physical Sciences: Physical and Chemical Change Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 10 Physical Sciences: Physical and chemical change
standard_text: Physical changes and chemical changes; the conservation of atoms and mass; writing and balancing chemical equations; the law of constant composition. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 10, Chemistry: Physical and chemical change)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): physical and chemical changes, word and balanced equations, and the conservation of mass. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: In a chemical change new substances form.
key_sub: Atoms are conserved, so equations must balance.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a physical change (melting, dissolving) no new substance forms and the change is usually easy to reverse. In a chemical change (burning, rusting) bonds are broken and new bonds form, making new substances, with energy taken in or given out.

Atoms are not created or destroyed, so the total mass stays the same in a closed system. A balanced equation has the same number of each kind of atom on both sides; change only the coefficients, never the formulae.

Example

Balance: H₂ + O₂ → H₂O

Count O atoms first.

Answer: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O

Example

Is dissolving sugar a physical or a chemical change?

No new substance forms.

Answer: a physical change

Common mistakes

  • Changing a formula to balance an equation.
  • Thinking mass is lost when something burns (gases escape).
  • Thinking all colour changes are chemical.

faq.q: What is the law of constant composition?
faq.a: A compound always contains the same elements in the same ratio by mass, for example water is always 1 : 8 hydrogen to oxygen.

faq.q: Why does a burning candle seem to lose mass?
faq.a: The products, carbon dioxide and water vapour, escape into the air.
